I will put all 7.0 mu into cotton again this year, because that is the crop I know best and it fits my land, my experience, and the well irrigation I can rely on. Since some family members work off-farm and there are only 3 people in the household, I will keep the system simple and familiar instead of trying to divide the land into different crops. I will use improved cotton seed rather than traditional seed, because I want steadier emergence and better yield without making management too complicated. At the start of the season, I will plough the land so the soil is loosened well and the roots can go down better. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate amount of nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium together, because cotton needs balanced nutrition and I do not want too much vegetative growth. Since I have a well, I will plan several irrigations during the key growth periods, but not too many, because cotton does not need constant watering. I will also spray pesticides a few times during the season when pressure is highest, because protecting the crop is necessary if I want stable production. With this kind of management on my 7.0 mu, I will aim for a solid, realistic yield rather than chasing an unusually high one.
